title: Canonical comparison with right derived tower limit
statement: Let M be abelian with countable products, inverse-sequence limits, unbounded derived categories and K-injective resolutions of tower complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let F be an endofunctor on cochain complexes with descents T on D(M) and S on D(Tow(M)), and specified localization isomorphisms e and eS. For a right derived pair (RF, eta) of ordinary tower limit [def-weil-strict-roos-model], the right derivation remains right derived after T. The ordinary limit comparison, whose n-th projection is F(pi_n), induces a natural comparison beta: T RF Q -> RF Q tower(F). For any quasi-isomorphic K-injective resolutions s:X->I and q:tower(F)(I)->J, there are pinned isomorphisms dI,dJ with dI RF(Qs)=eta_I and dJ RF(Q(tower(F)(s)q))=eta_J; beta_X=T(dI^-1)e_limI Q(theta)dJ, where theta has n-th projection F(pi_n)q_n. If F preserves quasi-isomorphisms, these formulas hold for all such resolutions. The comparison satisfies the whole augmentation equation for every strict cone. It is natural under transformations F->G and T->Tprime compatible with e, provided G preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The pointwise product comparison b has projections F(pr_n)q_n and commutes with one minus transition. All right-derived universality and localization isomorphisms are hypotheses; none is replaced by an arbitrary existence witness.

proof.text: Identify ordinary limits of complex-valued towers with termwise limits by their universal cones. The resulting functor factors through homotopy. Quasi-isomorphisms between K-injective towers are homotopy equivalences, so their limits become invertible after localization. The K-injective derivability structure therefore makes eta_I invertible and makes the right derivation absolute under any postcomposition.

proof.text: Apply the right-derived universal property to e followed by Q of the ordinary limit comparison and eta on tower(F). The resulting beta satisfies the universal unit equation. On resolutions, cancel the invertible units and the localized quasi-isomorphisms to obtain the formula with dI and dJ. On a strict cone, compose the same unit equation with its limit lift; the defining projections identify the two augmentation maps.

proof.text: For naturality in F, first cancel T(eta_I) on a K-injective tower. The ordinary-limit square is checked by projections and naturality of F->G. The universal unit equation identifies both composites. Resolve an arbitrary tower K-injectively and cancel the image of that quasi-isomorphism to extend the equality.

theorem comparison_resolution
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor η (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ M) (.up ℤ))]
    (hF : ∀ (X Y : CochainComplex M ℤ) (f : X ⟶ Y), QuasiIso f → QuasiIso (F.map f))
    (X I J : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ M) ℤ) (s : X ⟶ I) (q : (tower F).obj I ⟶ J)
    [QuasiIso s] [I.IsKInjective] [QuasiIso q] [J.IsKInjective] :
    ∃ (dI : DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (limit I.asFunctor) ≅
        RF.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj X))
      (dJ : DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (limit J.asFunctor) ≅
        RF.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj ((tower F).obj X))),
      dI.hom ≫ RF.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map s) = η.app I ∧
      dJ.hom ≫ RF.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map ((tower F).map s ≫ q)) = η.app J ∧
      (comparison F T S e eS RF η).app X =
        T.map dI.inv ≫ e.hom.app (limit I.asFunctor) ≫
          DerivedCategory.Q.map (limitComparisonMap F I J q) ≫ dJ.hom
